note: Track ii-v-i, step 2: the ii–V–i in minor, heard beside the major one, then its roots and the raised 7th inside its V chord tapped on a staff, then named by number without looking. Chords are chord tokens (ii°7 for the half-diminished chord), counted the long way where the staff can ring their roots, and the key is moves with a {{?key}} line on what stays the same.

exercise.title: The ii–V–i in minor
exercise.why: The minor ii–V–i moves its roots the same way as the major one and changes two colours, a half-diminished ii and a minor home chord, while the V stays a dominant 7 because minor borrows a raised 7th for it.

cells.text:
Press Play on the first backing track below to hear the ii–V–I in {{=key}} major. Then stop it and press Play on the second backing track below to hear the ii–V–i in its relative minor.
Listen for the two chords that change colour: the first chord of the minor one is half-diminished and its home chord is minor, while the middle chord is a dominant 7 in both.

{{chord:ii°7}} is the 2nd chord of the minor key, built on {{2}}. {{chord:V7}} is the 5th chord, built on {{5}}, and {{chord:i7}} is the 1st chord, built on {{1}}.
Press Play below to start the backing track again. Tap the root of each chord on the staff under it as its box lights, then tap {{7}} in the {{chord:V7}} bar and {{1}} in the {{chord:i7}} bar. {{7}} is the raised 7th of harmonic minor and the 3rd of {{chord:V7}}, a half step under home.
Practice until your tap on {{1}} lands with the chord.

Press Play below to start the backing track. Look away from the chord boxes and call out 2, 5 or 1 on each change, then look back to check.
Practice until the home chord arrives where you expect it.
{{?key}}In another key the chords have other names, and the order of colours is the same: half-diminished, dominant 7, minor.
